source.title: A Negative Result on Cross-Model Activation Transfer in a Pythia Multi-Hop Setting

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a post-hoc linear map between cross-model activations enables useful transfer, using downstream injection outcomes rather than only representational similarity measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports offline alignment scores and downstream results for activation-injection conditions. It also reports comparisons against no-injection and natural-language relay. Related-work findings are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study fits a linear map from Pythia-160M to Pythia-410M hidden states and then substitutes the mapped states into the frozen receiver. It reports both the offline fit and the downstream loss. The specific argument is that a high offline linear fit does not make representations interchangeable. This bears directly on V4, and the T5 argument outweighs T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also attribute the residual failure after scale correction mainly to direction or distribution error rather than norm mismatch. They stress the result is scoped to one pair, task and layer with a frozen, weak (<10% baseline) receiver.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a post-hoc linear activation translator followed by inference-time injection and downstream multi-hop answering; this differs from similarity-based convergence measurements and tests causal use in one model pair.
record.method_sensitivity: Injection type and strength matter: low-strength additive injection is near baseline, partial blending performs below baseline, and replacement remains harmful after norm correction. The study uses one fixed injection depth and one task protocol.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-strength additive injection of mapped sender states gives no stable gain over no-injection or text relay. The CIs cross zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearly mapped cross-model activations do not carry usable task information to a frozen receiver at inference time.

fits_no_version.finding: Correctly paired mapped states perform no better than shuffled or random same-norm states when substituted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High offline linear alignment between models does not imply that sample-specific mapped states are functionally meaningful to the receiver.

record.problems: Evidence is scoped to one Pythia sender-receiver pair, one direction, one task family, and one fixed injection depth. The receiver is not adapted, baseline word-boundary accuracy is below 10%, and metrics are automatic. The full-n shuffled control retains 13 self-fallback samples per seed, though a strict matched control removes them.
record.rows_left_out: No reported primary or legacy containment condition was left out. Normalized exact match is omitted because the paper says it is zero for every condition and it is not the main interpretive metric.

untested.parts: Only one linear map, one direction and one model pair (same family, different size) were tested. Not tested: other pairs or architectures, stitching with trained layers, relative representations, unpaired mapping, other layers.
No scale sweep and no comparison of convergence across models.
Seeds are run replications, not independently trained networks.
No variation of similarity metrics or of in- versus out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of causes of alignment or of a plateau.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's scope-based limits_scope label was dropped; unexamined conditions are listed as untested instead. Replacement rows were recoded from reversed to absent, because the version's effect (little-loss mapping) is absent rather than inverted. The contrast between offline cosine 0.97 and functional failure also bears loosely on V6: whether convergence appears depends on the measure, offline fit versus causal use. However, no similarity-metric settings were varied, so V6 is left untested. The Pythia pair shares architecture, tokenizer and training data, a best case for V4. The very low baseline accuracy limits how much loss could be observed.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability and no test of convergence across independently trained models as they grow.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
Seeds are used for stochastic-condition replications; the study does not compare representations from independently trained same-architecture models across initializations.

Tests one post-hoc linear bridge and inference-time activation injection in one Pythia model pair. Does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or general interchangeability across models and tasks.
No comparison of interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
Does not vary similarity measures or their settings, or test out-of-distribution inputs. It reports normalized-space alignment and downstream outcomes under one task protocol.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or whether representational alignment plateaus across scale.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M

rows.subject: Pythia-410M
